source_text: Gratia autem non eodem confertur modo, ut peccatis aeque admota singulis crebro repetatur; sed infusa semel uno virtutis suae impetu atque compendio diversa et plurima delet crimina. Ideo ait: Ex multis delictis in iustificationem [n340] , id est ex multis delictis liberatos homines ad gloriam perducit iustificationis indultae. Non ergo hic unum Adae peccatum, ut suspicaris, intellegit, sed ad hoc solum numerum admovit unius et plurium, ut ad laudem gratiae respiceret, quia non quoties peccatum ab unoquoque mortalium fuerat, totiens etiam frequentaretur gratia, quasi baptismata singula nisi peccatis singulis non possint mederi.
pass_a_gloss: But grace is not conferred in the same way, so that equally applied to single sins it would be frequently repeated; but poured in once by one impulse and shortcut of its virtue it deletes diverse and very many crimes. Therefore he says: From many offenses into justification, that is, human beings freed from many offenses it leads through unto the glory of an indulged justification. He therefore does not here understand one sin of Adam, as you suspect, but moved the number of one and of more only toward this, that it would look toward the praise of grace, because not as often as there had been sin by each of mortals, so often also would grace be frequented, as if single baptisms cannot heal except single sins.

lemmas.lexica: LS delictum; Blaise Rom 5 delictum vs donum
LS iustificatio; Blaise forensic making-just, not later system
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: Grace, however, is not conferred in the same way, repeatedly applied to each sin individually. Instead, poured in once, it wipes away many different crimes in a single concentrated action of its power. That is why he says, ‘From many offenses to justification’ (Romans 5:16): it leads human beings freed from many offenses to the glory of justification bestowed on them. Therefore he does not here mean Adam’s single sin, as you suppose. He uses the numbers one and many solely to praise grace: grace need not be repeated as often as each mortal person has sinned, as though individual baptisms could heal only individual sins.

choices.why: Paul's delictum of the one man; an act, not a nature.
Paul's iustificatio vitae; keep forensic making-just, not a later systematic slogan as default.
